claims.text: AECOPD: effective; give concurrently or alternating with beta-agonists.
claims.quote: Ipratropium, a short-acting anticholinergic, is effective in acute COPD exacerbations and should be given concurrently or alternating with beta-agonists.
claims.locator: Medication Therapy in Acute COPD Exacerbation › Anticholinergic agents

claims.text: Long-acting anticholinergics are not studied for exacerbations (kept for prevention/maintenance).
claims.quote: The use of longer-acting anticholinergics for the treatment of acute COPD exacerbations has not been studied, and their use is generally reserved for the exacerbation prevention (or maintenance therapy).
claims.locator: Medication Therapy in Acute COPD Exacerbation › Anticholinergic agents

claims.text: AECOPD dose: 0.25–0.5 mg by nebulizer or 2 MDI puffs every 4 to 6 h.
claims.quote: Dosage is 0.25 to 0.5 mg by nebulizer or 2 inhalations (17 to 18 mcg of drug delivered per puff) by metered-dose inhaler every 4 to 6 hours.
claims.locator: Medication Therapy in Acute COPD Exacerbation › Anticholinergic agents

claims.text: CI: hypersensitivity to ipratropium or to atropine or its derivatives.
claims.quote: Hypersensitivity to ipratropium bromide or other ATROVENT HFA components Hypersensitivity to atropine or any of its derivatives

claims.text: Not for initial treatment of acute bronchospasm needing rapid rescue.
claims.quote: Not indicated for the initial treatment of acute episodes of bronchospasm where rescue therapy is required for rapid response ( 5.1 )

claims.text: Other anticholinergic drugs: additive anticholinergic effects; avoid the combination.
claims.quote: Anticholinergics: May interact additively with concomitantly used anticholinergic medications. Avoid administration of COMBIVENT RESPIMAT with other anticholinergic-containing drugs (7.1)

claims.text: Acute inhaled overdose is unlikely: ipratropium is poorly absorbed systemically.
claims.quote: Acute overdose by inhalation is unlikely since ipratropium bromide is not well absorbed systemically after inhalation or oral administration.
